big_idea: Two-way tally tables ROW-by-ROW capture TWO PIECES of information per data point.
learning_intention: We are learning to make a two-way tally table.
student_learning_goal: I can make a two-way tally table.
success_criteria: I can record answers in a 2-way table.
I can total each ROW and COLUMN.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dot and Tally — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Tally: I asked TWO questions: favourite snack AND favourite drink. Now I record BOTH answers per child! Dot opens: 'BOTH? Only one? Or NEITHER?' Tally adds: 'Row, Column, Cell!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dot and Tally puppets. 'Friends — yesterday Venn and Carroll. Today TWO-WAY TALLY TABLES.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write TWO-WAY TALLY on chart. 'Two-way tally = a table with rows AND columns. Each cell is the count of children who chose THIS row AND THIS column.'

Demo. Draw on chart:

          | Apple | Cookie
Milk      |       |
Water     |       |

'Ask: snack? Drink? Tally each child in BOTH cells!'

Example: 'Bea picks cookie + milk. Tally in cookie+milk cell.' || mark.
'Maple picks apple + water. Tally in apple+water cell.' | mark.

More examples. Tally 5 students. Show row totals and column totals.

'Tally says — every CHILD = 1 tally in 1 cell. Row total = how many for that DRINK. Column total = how many for that SNACK.'

'Today YOU survey 2 questions and tally.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: tally 6 children's snack + drink choices in 2x2 table.
Three stations. A: Use a survey card and tally 8 classmates. B: Total rows + columns. C: Make own 2-question survey.

steps.teacher_prompt: Show: row total = drink totals; column = snack totals.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their two-way tables for the same survey data. Class compares: 'Did you label rows the same? Did you get the same joint counts?' Cite English (1993) cross-classification — table format MUST preserve joint counts regardless of row/column choice.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tally: 'Different headers, same data — but the JOINT COUNTS must match.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children stand in 2x2 grid by their answers.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: asks 2 questions; tallies in correct cell; totals rows + columns.

consolidation.exit_routine: Detective Dot's table refrain — class chants: 'Row says ___. Column says ___. Cell says BOTH!' Each child fills one cell and reads it aloud as a joint count.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child tallies BOTH answers in TWO cells — repairing the double-count trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On two-way tally tables, the trap is the SAME cross-classification difficulty surfaced through a different display: child can name a row OR a column attribute but cannot trace a CELL to its joint (row, column) coordinate (Inhelder & Piaget 1964; English 1993 on 2-D matrices in young children).

Yesterday Lesson 1 sorted by two rules with Venn/Carroll. Today the same two-attribute thinking goes into a TABLE — rows are one attribute, columns the other, cells are the joint count. Lesson 3 builds bar graphs from this; Lesson 4 finds mode; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Bea picks cookie + milk. Child tallies '|' in cookie row, then '|' in milk row separately — 2 tallies total.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You tallied Bea TWICE. But Tally says — ONE child = ONE tally. Where do BOTH her answers cross?'

Guide. Find the cell where COOKIE row meets MILK column. Place tally THERE. Erase the duplicates.

Generalise. 'Two-way tables work by INTERSECTION. Each cell = HOW MANY chose that BOTH combination.'

If still doubling: provide a tally template with example arrows pointing to one cell only.

Long-term recovery: every two-way tally uses 'one child, one cell'.
common_misconceptions: Cells are independent. (Repair: cells are intersections.)
Row total = column total. (Repair: they're different sums.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child fills cells but ignores row/column labels: ALWAYS-VISIBLE labels, child reads the row label aloud before placing the tally; reads column label aloud second.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child confuses rows and columns: lay the table horizontally on the floor; child stands on a row and walks along columns to find the cell.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can find a cell but can't articulate joint count: drill 'this cell counts students who are BOTH ___ AND ___'; child re-says before recording.

parts_outline.task: Read a 2-way table. Find row and column totals.
Make your own 2-way survey at home.
